lines.show: On a long wooden boat on the Rhine, you can watch small dimples on the water.
lines.say: On a long wooden boat on the Rhine, you can watch small dimples on the water.

lines.show: Some last surprisingly long, drifting beside the boat.

lines.show: Each one casts a shadow on the riverbed: a dark spot inside a bright ring.
lines.say: Each one casts a shadow on the riverbed: a dark spot inside a bright ring.

lines.show: They are tiny whirlpools, and the rules they follow are the mathematics of the last two episodes.
lines.say: They are tiny whirlpools, and the rules they follow are the mathematics of the last two episodes.

lines.show: Dimples on the Rhine.

lines.show: A dimple is the top of a small whirlpool.

lines.show: Water spinning fast has low pressure, so the surface sags into a funnel a millimetre or two deep.
lines.say: Water spinning fast has low pressure, so the surface sags into a funnel a millimetre or two deep.

lines.show: The funnel is a lens. It spreads the sunlight in the middle and gathers it at the rim.
lines.say: The funnel is a lens. It spreads the sunlight in the middle, and gathers it at the rim.

lines.show: The bright ring is a caustic, where the light rays pile up.
lines.say: The bright ring is a caustic, where the light rays pile up.

lines.show: Spin in water is hard to destroy, so without friction a whirlpool would last forever.
lines.say: Spin in water is hard to destroy, so without friction a whirlpool would last forever.

lines.show: They often come in pairs. An oar stroke leaves a half ring of spinning water below the surface,

lines.show: and its two ends show up as dimples that spin opposite ways.

lines.show: The pair sails off together, and the closer the two are, the faster they go.

lines.show: The rule behind this is simple: each whirlpool is carried along by the swirl of all the others.
lines.say: The rule behind this is simple: each whirlpool is carried along by the swirl of all the others.

lines.show: Two that spin the same way chase each other around a circle.
lines.say: Two that spin the same way chase each other around a circle.

lines.show: Near a riverbank, a whirlpool slides along the bank, as if pushed by its mirror image.
lines.say: Near a riverbank, a whirlpool slides along the bank, as if pushed by its mirror image.

lines.show: And two pairs, one behind the other, play leapfrog.
lines.say: And two pairs, one behind the other, play leapfrog.

lines.show: Now the key idea. In the simplest model, surface water cannot be squashed,

lines.show: so any patch of it keeps its area as it flows.
lines.say: so any patch of it keeps its area as it flows.

lines.show: In two dimensions, keeping area is exactly what symplectic means.

lines.show: Draw a contour map of the stream function. The water flows along the contour lines,
